legend: You are playing the sandbox game Mathcraft. Each crafting table of level k%%ZSMJ0%% can produce all possible products obtained by multiplying two numbers between 1%%ZSMJ1%% and k%%ZSMJ2%%.

If you unroll the k%%ZSMJ3%%-th crafting table, you get the array [1⋅1,1⋅2,…,1⋅k,2⋅1,2⋅2,…,2⋅k,…,k⋅1,k⋅2,…,k⋅k]%%ZSMJ4%%. For example, for k=4%%ZSMJ5%%, the unrolled table is [1,2,3,4,2,4,6,8,3,6,9,12,4,8,12,16]%%ZSMJ6%%.
Your friend Bob crafted a (contiguous) subarray of one unrolled crafting table. This subarray is a1,a2,…,an%%ZSMJ7%%.

You want to know how skilled Bob is, so you want to find the minimum possible level of his crafting table. Specifically, you want to determine the smallest k%%ZSMJ8%% such that a1,a2,…,an%%ZSMJ9%% appears as a subarray of the k%%ZSMJ10%%-th unrolled table.

An array b%%ZSMJ11%% is a subarray of an array c%%ZSMJ12%% if b%%ZSMJ13%% can be obtained from c%%ZSMJ14%% by deleting several (possibly zero or all) elements from the beginning and several (possibly zero or all) elements from the end.
input: Each test contains multiple test cases. The first line contains the number of test cases t%%ZSMJ15%% (1≤t≤500%%ZSMJ16%%). The description of the test cases follows.
The first line of each test case contains a single integer n%%ZSMJ17%% (2≤n≤100%%ZSMJ18%%) — the length of the array a1,a2,…,an%%ZSMJ19%%.
The second line of each test case contains n%%ZSMJ20%% integers a1,a2,…,an%%ZSMJ21%% (1≤ai≤109%%ZSMJ22%%).
Note that there are no constraints on the sum of n%%ZSMJ23%% over all test cases.
output: For each test case, output a single line containing an integer: the smallest crafting table level k%%ZSMJ24%% such that the array a1,a2,…,an%%ZSMJ25%% appears as a contiguous subarray of the k%%ZSMJ26%%-th unrolled table. For the given input, such a k%%ZSMJ27%% always exists.
note: Explanation of sample 1. In the first test case, the array [4,6,8,10]%%ZSMJ28%% is a subarray of the 5%%ZSMJ29%%-th unrolled table, which is [1,2,3,4,5,2,4,6,8,10,…,5,10,15,20,25]%%ZSMJ30%%. There is no smaller valid k%%ZSMJ31%%, so the answer is 5%%ZSMJ32%%.
In the second test case, the array [8,3,6,9,12,4]%%ZSMJ33%% is a subarray of the 4%%ZSMJ34%%-th unrolled table, which is [1,2,3,4,2,4,6,8,3,6,9,12,4,8,12,16]%%ZSMJ35%%.
